reviews.name: phase16-spec-review
reviews.note: The watched window opened control streams (open passed observe, not observing), stale looking tab on window close, restored tab not streamed, a window closed during restore leaking, late reopens overriding a control move.

reviews.name: phase16-ponytail-review
reviews.note: Found the observe/observing bug first (as 'the watches chain does nothing'), plus small cuts (Notice init, shared test helpers, leave()).

reviews.name: phase16-e2e-review
reviews.note: Drove the bug in a throwaway XCUITest (p4 opened control) and confirmed the fix; asked for a key-only takeover test and a controller-closes-page test, both real gaps. ~3 min GUI lock.

reviews.name: phase16-spec-review-2
reviews.note: Side effects of round-1 fixes: a live-update reopen would grab another device's pane, a cancelled restore could still start default, a closed window kept its WindowContent able to open streams.

reviews.name: phase16-ponytail-review-2
reviews.note: Two cosmetic nits (padding, a duplicate assignment).

reviews.name: phase16-e2e-review-2
reviews.note: Asked to prove window 1 still controls before its page closes, and for race-safe waitForNonExistence after control changes. No GUI.

reviews.name: phase16-spec-review-3
reviews.note: Clean; one optional nit (rejected: SwiftUI cancels the window's task when the window goes).

reviews.name: phase16-e2e-review-3
reviews.note: The per-card take-back check could pass before the card was watching; moved after the observe stream is up.

notes: Rough screenshot sent at +24 min. ~20 min went into window restore: SwiftUI hands a restored window its scene storage after the first .task runs, AppKit had already saved full screen before a quit-time exit, and this Mac does not restore after a normal quit (default setting), so the check needed -NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows YES and XCUITest attached to an app started with open. A `git checkout` of one file to drop debug logging reverted all its phase changes (redone from the scripts). Overlapping windows made a raise click land on the wrong window; firstMatch silently followed the front window in one test until the final screenshots showed it.
